record_title: Sharp black-box robustness frontier for scalar Aitken-Steffensen acceleration
scientific_context: For a scalar global q-contraction, the exact worst-case fixed-point-error factor of one restarted Aitken-Steffensen cycle is 2q^2/((1-q)(1+2q)). Universal one-cycle error nonexpansion holds exactly through q=(1+sqrt(17))/8. For nondecreasing contractions the exact factor is q^2/(1-q^2), with threshold q=1/sqrt(2). Under only contraction information, two ordinary Picard evaluations have the smaller minimax factor q^2.
limitations: Scalar real global contractions and exact arithmetic only. The main theorem is a one-cycle fixed-point-error statement, with a repeated-cycle corollary only when the sharp factor is below one. It does not cover vector acceleration, floating-point stability, or imply long-run divergence above the universal nonexpansion threshold. Older Steffensen literature leaves residual historical-equivalence uncertainty.
